title: Lambda execution environment and lifecycle
hook: Each Lambda invocation runs in an ephemeral execution environment — reuse warm sandboxes for performance but never depend on in-memory state for correctness.

blocks.text: AWS Lambda creates an execution environment — a Firecracker microVM sandbox running your runtime and handler. After invoke completes, AWS may freeze the environment for reuse. Initialization code outside the handler runs once per environment. /tmp provides 512 MB to 10 GB ephemeral disk. Memory setting scales CPU proportionally.

entries.plainDefinition: Sandbox running one runtime instance until recycled.
entries.example: Warm pool reuses env for next invoke.

entries.plainDefinition: Writable scratch space 512MB-10GB based on memory config.
Code outside handler runs on cold start before first invoke.
entries.example: const client = new S3Client({}) outside handler.

entries.plainDefinition: 128 MB to 10 GB — also allocates proportional CPU.

blocks.text: Global variables and open connections persist on warm invokes — useful for SDK client reuse, dangerous for tenant data leakage. /tmp is not durable across all invocations. Timeout and memory directly affect bill and CPU.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: stateless handler, init outside handler for clients, /tmp scratch only, memory tunes CPU and cost.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Init
items.body: Runtime loads, top-level code runs — SDK clients, env validation.

items.title: Invoke
items.body: Handler receives event, processes, returns sync or async result.

items.title: Freeze
items.body: Environment frozen with memory state possibly preserved.

items.title: Recycle
items.body: AWS discards environment unpredictably — design stateless.

diagram.title: Execution environment reuse
diagram.source:
flowchart LR
  Cold[Cold start\ninit + handler] --> Freeze[Environment frozen]
  Freeze --> Warm[Warm invoke\nhandler only]
  Warm --> Freeze
  Freeze --> Recycle[Recycled\nstate lost]

snippet.label: Lambda function CloudFormation
snippet.code:
ProcessFn:
  Type: AWS::Lambda::Function
  Properties:
    Runtime: nodejs20.x
    Handler: index.handler
    MemorySize: 1024
    Timeout: 30
    EphemeralStorage:
      Size: 1024
    Environment:
      Variables:
        TABLE_NAME: !Ref OrdersTable
    Role: !GetAtt LambdaRole.Arn
snippet.explanation: Memory and timeout are primary tuning knobs. EphemeralStorage expands /tmp.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Storing user session in global variable — leaks across invocations on same environment. Writing audit trail only to /tmp. Huge deployment package slowing init.

blocks.text: Lambda extensions run alongside function for observability agents. SnapStart for Java reduces init. How to prove it in production: CloudWatch Max Memory Used vs configured memory, InitDuration on cold starts, X-Ray subsegments for init vs handler.

blocks.title: Tradeoffs at senior level
rows: More CPU — may reduce total cost
Lower cost same perf for many runtimes
Native deps must be arm built

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Relying on global state for correctness gets rejected. Strong answer: stateless handler, external store, init reuse for clients only.

interviewTakeaways: Execution environments are ephemeral — design handlers stateless.
Initialize SDK clients outside handler for warm performance.
/tmp is scratch only — not durable storage.
60s: Stateless handler. Init outside handler. /tmp ephemeral. Memory scales CPU. Never trust warm globals for tenant data.
Follow-up: when does AWS recycle an environment?
commonPitfalls: Global variable for per-user auth context — rejected (cross-tenant leak risk).
Strong answer: pass identity in event; store session in DynamoDB.
Assuming /tmp persists forever across all invokes.
512MB default /tmp for large file processing without raising EphemeralStorage.
